run.question: I'm investigating an error in trace TRACE-ERR-X9K2M. Check Elasticsearch and tell me which service failed and what the error was.

report.summary: Elasticsearch index app-245-apm-traces contains two documents for trace_id TRACE-ERR-X9K2M inside the authorized window (both at 2026-11-22T10:25:00Z). The failing service recorded in the trace is payment-gateway: span_id span-pay-err, operation authenticate_payment, http.status_code 503, duration_ms 5180, error.type ConnectionTimeout, error.message 'Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729'. Its stack trace shows payment_gateway's auth client posting to an auth_url with timeout=5.0 and timing out. The same trace contains the caller span from api-gateway (span_id span-gw-err, operation 'POST /api/payment', http.status_code 503, duration_ms 5234); the payment-gateway span's parent_span_id is span-gw-err, which is a supplied parent reference for exactly that one edge. So the error was a 503 caused by a connection timeout in payment-gateway's authentication call, propagated as a 503 on the api-gateway request. I did not establish where the timeout originated: the authentication dependency is named only as 'auth_url' with error code AUTH-4729, and neither payment-gateway nor api-gateway exists as a Deployment or Service in the queried cluster (the otel-demo topology has a differently named 'payment' service). Jaeger trace lookups and all Prometheus queries returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE in this Run, so the trace could not be corroborated in Jaeger and no error-rate or latency signal could be read; the otel-demo payment pod's logs showed no error-matching lines in the window. Root cause is left null because the evidence identifies the failing service and its error, but not one object where the fault originates and no object applying it.

claims.text: In index app-245-apm-traces, a span with trace_id TRACE-ERR-X9K2M at @timestamp 2026-11-22T10:25:00.050Z belongs to service payment-gateway (span_id span-pay-err, operation authenticate_payment, http.status_code 503, duration_ms 5180) and carries error.type ConnectionTimeout and error.message 'Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729'.

The payment-gateway span's error.stack_trace (index app-245-apm-traces) shows the timeout raised inside the payment gateway's auth client: /app/payment_gateway/handlers/payment_handler.py process_payment calls /app/payment_gateway/clients/auth_client.py authenticate, which does http_client.post(auth_url, json=payload, timeout=5.0); the recorded duration is 5180 ms.

The same trace TRACE-ERR-X9K2M contains an api-gateway span span-gw-err (operation 'POST /api/payment', http.status_code 503, duration_ms 5234, @timestamp 2026-11-22T10:25:00Z), and the payment-gateway span's parent_span_id is span-gw-err, i.e. the supplied parent reference makes api-gateway the parent of the failing payment-gateway span.

The queried cluster holds no Deployment and no Service named payment-gateway or api-gateway: the 24 Deployments and 29 Services at query time include the otel-demo 'payment' Deployment (ready 1, available 1) and 'payment' Service on port 8080, which are differently named entities from the payment-gateway service in the trace.

At query time all 24 Deployments in the cluster report readyReplicas equal to availableReplicas (e.g. otel-demo payment 1/1, checkout 1/1, frontend 1/1), and the pod list showed all otel-demo pods in phase Running and ready, with no OOMKilled/Evicted last termination reason (lastState.terminated.reason was 'Unknown' for otel-demo pods).

The only events inside the window were 2 Endpoints events with reason FailedToCreateEndpoint: 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-219/mariadb: endpoints "mariadb" already exists' at 2026-11-22T10:07:47Z and the same message for app-162/signup-service at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo defines fault flags including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), both with defaultVariant 'off'; these settings concern the otel-demo payment service, not the payment-gateway service in the trace, and no evidence in this Run shows either flag switched on.

The proximate trigger of the failure is a timeout toward an authentication dependency reached at auth_url: payment-gateway's client waited the full ~5 s then failed with ConnectionTimeout / AUTH-4729 and returned 503. The authentication service's name, namespace and health are not visible in the evidence, so this remains a hypothesis about where the fault originates.

The two FailedToCreateEndpoint events (app-219/mariadb, app-162/signup-service) were considered as a candidate cause of the 503 and rejected: they concern other namespaces and services, no event names payment-gateway, api-gateway or an auth service, and the trace error itself is a client-side connection timeout.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable in this Run: traces_list_services and traces_search for service 'payment' returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and traces_query_trace_by_id for 'TRACE-ERR-X9K2M' was refused with INVALID_PARAMS (the id is not a 32-character hex Jaeger trace id), so the trace could not be corroborated or expanded in Jaeger.

Prometheus was unreachable: metrics_range_query (traces_span_metrics_calls_total by service_name/status_code) and list_prometheus_rules both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or alert-firing signal could be read for payment-gateway or api-gateway, and no baseline is available for any latency comparison.

The authentication dependency is unidentified: the trace exposes only 'auth_url' and error code AUTH-4729, with no host name, service name or namespace, and the http.request.body / http.response.body / stack trace were cut at 2000 characters.

The otel-demo payment pod log query returned no error-matching lines in the window (152 lines read, 0 matched, status no_data), so no application-log evidence ties the otel-demo payment service to this failure, and no partial logs from a previous container existed (0 lines).

Whether payment-gateway and api-gateway are Kubernetes workloads at all could not be confirmed: no Deployment or Service of those names exists in the queried cluster, so their pod status, restart history and termination reasons are unknown.
Change history integration is not available in this Run, so no change or restart could be correlated with the error.
Only 2 documents carried trace_id TRACE-ERR-X9K2M in the sole index app-245-apm-traces; other spans of that trace, if any, are unknown.
next_steps: Look up trace TRACE-ERR-X9K2M in Jaeger (valid 32-hex id) once the Jaeger backend is reachable, to enumerate all spans and confirm whether any span belongs to an authentication service.

Find the configured auth_url for the payment gateway (e.g. payment-gateway service config/env) to identify the authentication dependency, then check that dependency's own error and latency signals in Prometheus.

Once Prometheus is reachable, query traces_span_metrics_calls_total by service_name and status_code and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds for payment-gateway/api-gateway to establish whether the AUTH-4729 timeout is isolated to this trace or systemic.
Confirm whether payment-gateway/api-gateway run outside this cluster; if they run here under other names, inspect those pods' status, previous-container termination reasons and logs for AUTH-4729.
